summary: The record already exists live but is missing from Terraform state, so reconcile it with an approved import.
findings: The existing record already exists in inventory; the state evidence has no cloudflare_record.app binding, so the create plan risks a duplicate.
Preserve terraform state pull as state-before-import.json; the backend is unchanged and no configuration change is needed.
actions: Sequence: terraform fmt -check; terraform validate; (umask 077 && terraform plan -lock=true -lock-timeout=5m -out=pre-import.tfplan); terraform state pull > state-before-import.json.
After import approval: terraform import -lock=true -lock-timeout=5m cloudflare_record.app zone-demo/demo-record-17.
Then run (umask 077 && terraform plan -lock=true -lock-timeout=5m -out=post-import.tfplan); apply requires a separate second approval.
Rollback after approval with terraform state rm cloudflare_record.app for a wrong association, or set TTL back to 600 and review a new non-destructive plan.
checks: Expect an in-place TTL-only change from 600 to 300 with no create/destroy.
After approved apply, verify the authoritative nameserver and a public resolver such as 1.1.1.1.
message: Next gate: approve only the import after state backup and plan review; apply remains separately gated.
